newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says comfortable with exchange rate.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says comfortable with exchange rate.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Central Bank governor said on Friday that he was comfortable with the current exchange rate of the rupee and would not let the currency depreciate unnecessarily.

"We are happy with the exchange rate. If our inflation is higher than world levels we will allow the rupee to depreciate in the market. That does not mean we will deliberately depreciate it to increase our competitive advantage," Amarananda Jayawardena told Reuters in an interview.
He said there were no serious complaints from exporters about the exchange rate.
"Large changes in the exchange rate are not good for the country as we are more trade dependent than others," he said.
The Sri Lankan rupee has been largely static at around 58.40 to the dollar this week. The currency was trading at 58.44 to the dollar at 0820 GMT.
A recent Reuters poll of foreign exchange dealers showed the rupee, which has lost three percent of its value since January, ending the year at 60.85 to the dollar.
